name: Spain
tagline: One accreditation, UNEDasiss, unlocks almost every Spanish university
summary: Spain has a single gateway for IB students: an accreditation from UNED called UNEDasiss. It turns your IB into a Spanish admission grade on a 14-point scale, and public universities then admit by rank on that number. You can raise the grade by sitting extra subject exams called PCE. Public university fees are low — roughly €1,000–€1,250 a year for an EU student at Carlos III — but English-taught bachelor's degrees are concentrated in a handful of universities, several of them private and much more expensive.
whyConsider: One digital accreditation (UNEDasiss) is accepted by most Spanish universities, so you do not repeat the paperwork for each one
Public university tuition for EU students is genuinely low: around €1,015–€1,241 a year at Universidad Carlos III for 2026/27
You can actively raise your admission grade to 14 points by sitting PCE subject exams, so a mid-range IB is not the end of the story
IB Diploma holders do not need to homologate their diploma — UNEDasiss replaces that
Strong English-taught options in Madrid and Barcelona, plus real alternatives in Pamplona, Bilbao and Segovia
watchOuts: The timetable is brutal for an IB student: the ordinary PCE exams fall in late May 2026-style windows, which for the May 2027 session collides directly with your IB exams
Competitive degrees (Medicine, some engineering) are decided by cut-off grades that can sit above 12 out of 14, so a good IB alone may not be enough
Which PCE subjects count double for your degree is decided by each university's weighting table (ponderaciones), and those change year to year
The private universities (IE, Navarra, ESADE, Deusto, Comillas) run their own admission with their own tests and interviews, and charge many times the public fee
Spanish access rules have been changing (Real Decreto 534/2024 as amended by RD 482/2025). Re-check the rules that apply to 2027 entry rather than trusting an older guide.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: 24 points (the full IB Diploma pass). Reported as the minimum for an equivalent Spanish grade to be issued; this figure comes from secondary guidance and was not confirmed on a UNED page during research.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: PCE subject exams, not HL/SL, are what Spanish universities use to check subject depth. Where a university does recognise IB subjects directly, HL subjects are the ones normally accepted for weighting — not verified on an official page.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: UNEDasiss converts your IB record into a Spanish 'nota de acceso' between 5 and 10. That can be raised to a maximum 'nota de admisión' of 14 by adding up to 4 points from weighted subject exams (each weighted subject contributes up to 2 points, at a coefficient of 0.1 or 0.2 set by the destination university).
notes: In the UNEDasiss application you select country/system 'Europa' then 'Programa del Diploma IB', and study type 'Estudios secundarios del Anexo I del reglamento'.

The one service you must tick is 'Calificación para Admisión Universidad española'. Everything else (modalidad de bachillerato, PCE, language accreditation) is optional but often required by the university you are aiming at — check its criteria first.

Documents to send: a copy of your passport or ID, a compulsed copy of the IB Diploma, and a compulsed copy of the grades for your last two years. The IB Diploma is a Swiss document, so it does not need an apostille — a copy compulsed at a Spanish embassy or consulate is enough.

IB holders access Spanish universities through UNEDasiss without homologating the diploma. Real Decreto 412/2014 established that IB and European Baccalaureate holders are admitted on the same criteria as Spanish students.

Some universities, notably Universidad de Navarra, run their own IB pathway with fixed minimum IB scores per faculty (for example 37 points for Medicine with HL Biology and Chemistry at 6, 34 for Engineering with HL Maths at 6) plus an interview and conditional admission on predicted grades — you still need the UNED accreditation on top.
A widely repeated conversion (an IB subject grade of 4 counting as a Spanish 7, a 2 as a Spanish 5) appears in commercial guidance but was not verified on a UNED page. Treat it as unconfirmed.

portal.name: UNEDasiss (accreditation) then each region's preinscripción system

deadlines.label: UNEDasiss accreditation application window
deadlines.year: opens annually — 2027 dates not yet published
deadlines.notes: UNEDasiss states the online accreditation request opens on 4 February and closes on 1 December each year. Apply early: the accreditation has to exist before the university preinscripción closes in June/July. Confirm the 2027 dates when they are published.

deadlines.label: PCE registration — ordinary (May/June) call
deadlines.notes: Through a UNED collaborating centre the window opened earlier, on 18 February 2026, and closed on the same date. The 2027 equivalent is likely to fall in the same weeks but must be re-checked.

deadlines.label: PCE exams — ordinary (May/June) call
deadlines.notes: This window overlaps the IB examination session. Plan carefully, and check whether an overseas UNED centre can sit you on a different day. Re-check the 2027 calendar.

deadlines.label: PCE registration — extraordinary (September) call
deadlines.notes: This is the realistic call for an IB student who wants to sit PCE after the IB exams, but it lands after most first-round university preinscripción closes, so you may only be competing for second-round places.

deadlines.label: PCE exams — extraordinary (September) call
deadlines.notes: Results were reported as published by 20 September in the September call; this publication date was not confirmed on a UNED page.

steps: Before anything else, look up the admission criteria of the universities you want: which UNEDasiss services they demand, and which subjects they weight for your degree.
Create a UNEDasiss account and submit the accreditation request, selecting 'Europa' → 'Programa del Diploma IB' and ticking 'Calificación para Admisión Universidad española'.
Send the documents: passport copy, compulsed copy of the IB Diploma, compulsed copy of your last two years' grades.
If you need more than 10 points, register for PCE exams in the subjects your target degree weights — normally four to six subjects.
Sit the PCE exams and let UNEDasiss compute your nota de admisión out of 14.

Apply through the preinscripción system of the region you want (Madrid, Catalonia, Andalusia and the rest each run their own) or directly to a private university, quoting your UNEDasiss accreditation.
Accept your place and enrol (matrícula), which at public universities means paying per credit.
application.selectionNotes: Public universities admit strictly by rank on the nota de admisión against a published cut-off (nota de corte) for each degree, which moves each year with demand. Private universities (IE, Navarra, ESADE, Deusto, Comillas) run their own selection: own admission test, essays and interview, usually with rolling rounds from the autumn.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A real but concentrated offer. Most English-taught bachelors sit at a handful of universities — IE, Carlos III, Pompeu Fabra, Navarra, ESADE, Autònoma de Barcelona, Deusto, Comillas — rather than being spread across the system. No official national count was found during research.
language.englishProof: UNEDasiss offers a language-accreditation service, and universities generally accept IB English A or B; the accepted grade or IELTS/TOEFL alternative varies by university and was not verified institution by institution.
notes: Even on an English-taught degree, Spanish matters for everything outside the lecture theatre, and many 'English-taught' degrees are partly bilingual.
In Catalonia and the Basque Country, Catalan or Basque may appear in parts of a supposedly Spanish-language degree. Ask which language each module is actually delivered in.

tuitionEuEea.value: Public universities charge per credit and the price is set regionally. Universidad Carlos III de Madrid 2026/27: €16.92 per credit for social sciences and law (€1,015.20 for a 60-credit year), €19.43 for engineering and maths (€1,165.80), €20.68 for biomedical engineering and neuroscience (€1,240.80), plus small administrative and insurance fees. Private universities are far higher and set their own fees.

costs.applicationFee: UNEDasiss charges per service requested (accreditation, admission-grade calculation, each PCE subject). The official price table is published as an image and could not be read during research, so no euro figure is given here. UNEDasiss states fees are payable even if a service is later refused, and are not reducible or waivable.
notes: The UC3M price page states those rates apply to EU students and Spanish nationals. Non-EU pricing is set by each autonomous region and was not verified during research, so it is left blank rather than guessed.

Private universities — IE, Navarra, ESADE, Deusto, Comillas — publish their own fees, typically many times the public rate. Those figures could not be fetched from their official pages during research and are deliberately left out.
Repeating a course costs more: Spanish public universities charge a higher price per credit on second and later enrolments in the same subject.

funding: Danish SU may be taken abroad for a full degree if the programme is approved — check su.dk before committing.
Spanish state 'becas generales' from the Ministerio de Educación are means-tested and generally open to EU students meeting residence conditions; the conditions were not verified during research.
Regional grants from the autonomous communities, which vary a lot between Madrid, Catalonia, Navarre and the Basque Country.
Private universities run their own substantial merit scholarships; IE, Navarra and ESADE all publish scholarship schemes tied to academic record and, at some, the IB score.
Erasmus+ for an exchange year inside the degree.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full labour-market access in Spain with no permit. Non-EU students hold a study residence permit that allows limited part-time work, but the exact hour limit was not verified on an official page during research.
residency: As a Danish citizen you travel on your passport or ID card. If you stay more than three months you register in the Registro Central de Extranjeros and receive a green EU registration certificate with a NIE number. You need the NIE for a bank account, a phone contract and usually for enrolment itself, so apply for an appointment as soon as you arrive. You will also normally register on the local padrón at the town hall.
housing: Spain relies heavily on the private rental market and shared flats (piso compartido). University halls (colegios mayores and residencias) exist and are mostly private, catered and expensive. Madrid and Barcelona are tight and pricey; Segovia, Pamplona and Bilbao are far easier. Start looking in June or July, and expect to be asked for a deposit plus one or two months in advance.
healthcare: Bring a European Health Insurance Card, which covers you as a visiting EU citizen. Once you register as a resident you can normally be enrolled with a local health centre and assigned a doctor; private universities often bundle or require private insurance instead.

institutions.name: IE University
institutions.englishBachelors: Almost the entire bachelor portfolio is taught in English
institutions.note: The most international private option in Spain, with its own admission test and interview rather than the UNEDasiss cut-off route; fees were not verifiable during research.

institutions.name: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid
institutions.englishBachelors: A substantial English-taught offer including Economics, International Studies, Aerospace Engineering and Data Science
institutions.note: The clearest value-for-money option in Spain: English-taught degrees at public prices of roughly €1,000–€1,250 a year.

institutions.name: Universitat Pompeu Fabra
institutions.englishBachelors: Some fully English-taught bachelors, including Global Studies
institutions.note: Small, research-intensive and consistently the top-ranked Spanish university for economics and social science.

institutions.name: Universidad de Navarra
institutions.englishBachelors: A limited English-taught offer, with several bilingual degrees
institutions.note: Private, Catholic, strongly ranked for Medicine and Communication, and one of the few Spanish universities with a published IB-specific admission pathway.

institutions.name: ESADE
institutions.city: Barcelona and Sant Cugat del Vallès
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught bachelor in Business Administration, plus bilingual law and AI-focused degrees
institutions.note: A well-regarded private business and law school with its own admission process, entrance test and interview.

institutions.name: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught bachelors
institutions.note: A large public research university on a self-contained campus outside Barcelona, cheaper to live near than the city centre.

institutions.name: Universidad de Deusto
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-taught and trilingual bachelors, mainly in business and international relations
institutions.note: A private Jesuit university in the Basque Country with a strong international-relations tradition and a genuinely different city to live in.

institutions.name: Universidad Pontificia Comillas (ICADE)
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught and bilingual bachelors in business, law and international relations
institutions.note: Madrid's other well-known private business-and-law school, with a strong record for graduate employment in Spain.

institutions.name: Universidad Autónoma de Madrid
institutions.note: One of Spain's strongest public research universities, on a green campus north of Madrid.

institutions.name: Universitat de Barcelona
institutions.englishBachelors: A small English-taught offer at bachelor level
institutions.note: Spain's largest and most research-productive public university, but mostly teaching in Catalan and Spanish at bachelor level.

institutions.name: Universidad Complutense de Madrid
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited at bachelor level; some bilingual groups
institutions.note: Huge, central and historic, with some of the highest cut-off grades in Spain for Medicine.

institutions.name: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya
institutions.note: Catalonia's main technical university, and the usual route into engineering in Barcelona.
